# Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq fall as chip stocks sell off, bond yields rattle markets

[Grace O'Donnell](https://finance.yahoo.com/author/grace-odonnell)· Editor, Special Projects

Updated Tue, August 18, 2026 at 4:14 PM EDT1 min read

- [CL=F \\
+0.73%](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CL%3DF/ "CL=F")

- [^IXIC \\
  -1.33%](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EIXIC/ "^IXIC")

- [^DJI \\
  -0.22%](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EDJI/ "^DJI")

- [^GSPC \\
  -0.69%](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGSPC/ "^GSPC")


US stocks fell on Tuesday as tech stocks sold off and elevated oil prices and government bond yields weighed on markets.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( [^IXIC](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EIXIC/)) fell 1.3%, leading the major indexes lower. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( [^DJI](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EDJI/)) declined by 0.2%, while the S&P 500 ( [^GSPC](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGSPC/)) pulled back by 0.6%, extending losses after [a downbeat start to the trading week.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-monday-august-17-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-oil-treasurys-094421171.html)

7,691.76 -53.30 (-0.69%)

At close: August 18 at 4:38:24 PM EDT

^GSPC^DJI ^IXIC

Oil prices climbed to their highest level in over two weeks after President Trump said he intends to inflict more economic pain on Iran and [threatened to "bomb" Oman](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/well-bomb-the-s-out-of-them-trump-threatens-oman-as-it-reportedly-moves-toward-a-deal-with-iran-155621451.html) if it interferes with the US's plans for the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude ( [BZ=F](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BZ=F/)) futures, the international benchmark, traded near $91 per barrel, and US benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude futures ( [CL=F](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CL=F/)) rose to $84 per barrel as the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve plunged to its [lowest level since 1982](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/article/the-strategic-petroleum-reserve-hasnt-been-this-low-since-reagan-was-filling-it-in-1982-critics-wonder-how-low-is-too-low-180740733.html).

Rising oil, [an AI borrowing spree](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/ai-driving-treasury-yields-just-093000747.html?.tsrc=372&ncid=crm_-2240951-20260817-0--A&bt_user_id_proof=MYmKMtbFxMgc3XAqiUPZn33g1jr6OV2xnexP285aBXsSw1VyJkYotJmm3SffjYrrKaRDUhgvmsyD2O3a1twjSTenUJjfJjRupbWoA4Ad%2Feb6NbGeLUvzvsdQHtCVhdNL&bt_ts_proof=1787005901660), and concerns over government borrowing have also lifted bond yields globally in recent days. The 10-year Treasury yield ( [^TNX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ETNX/)) eased somewhat but remained elevated at 4.70%, and the 30-year yield ( [^TYX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ETYX/)) held near a 19-year high.

Earnings, meanwhile, have supported equities so far this reporting season. While the second quarter reporting period has slowed, Home Depot's ( [HD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HD/)) stock was little changed after reporting an improvement in sales for the second quarter as customers leaned toward smaller projects over the summer, and Klarna ( [KLAR](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/KLAR/)) [stock plunged on a trimmed outlook.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/klarna-stock-plunges-20-on-trimmed-guidance-as-german-retail-sales-slow-141517463.html)

# Stock Market Today (Aug. 18, 2026): Nasdaq, S&P 500 slip as 30-year Treasury hits highest yield in nearly two decades

Investors are concerned after President Trump said he would not try to revive a stalled truce with Iran.

Aug 18, 2026 7:45 PM EDT

- ![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/MTkyMjg3NDQwMDY3NjM0NzM0/rob-lenihan.jpg?profile=w256&ar=1-1)


By [Rob Lenihan](https://www.thestreet.com/author/rob-lenihan) and [Noah Weidner](https://www.thestreet.com/author/noah-weidner)

Follow

1

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

![NYSE Traders](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTQ3MTM5/nyse-traders-2.jpg?profile=w2560&ar=4-3)[xPACIFICA/Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/photo/traders-work-in-front-of-computers-on-the-floor-of-royalty-free-image/521763968?phrase=NYSE&searchscope=image%2Cfilm&slot=44&adppopup=true)

_This live blog is refreshed throughout the day with the latest updates from the market._ **_To find the latest [Stock Market Today](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/stock-market-today) threads, [click here](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/stock-market-today)._**

**Happy Tuesday.** Stocks fell Tuesday and oil prices climbed amid rising tensions between the U.S. and Iran.

President Donald Trump said he would not try to revive a stalled truce with Iran.

A memorandum of understanding the U.S. and Iran signed in June that gave the two sides a 60-day window to negotiate a lasting peace deal technically expired Monday. When Trump was asked if he would seek an extension, he replied, “No,” [Bloomberg reported](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-18/trump-takes-hard-line-on-iran-as-hormuz-standoff-drags-on).

The ceasefire had already been repeatedly violated, with intermittent clashes continuing, and both sides had declared it defunct.

Stocks [closed lower Monday](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-aug-17-2026) as oil prices rose and the 30-year Treasury [yield](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/y/yield) tested multi-decade highs due to concerns about the Iran conflict.

Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst with Capital.com, said renewed tensions in the Middle East and subsequently higher oil prices weighed on [Wall Street](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/w/wall-street).

“The bellicosity was dialed up by the Trump administration to kick off the week, with US President Trump putting up a nonchalant front about the prospect of extending the existing memorandum of understanding with Iran, while threatening to bomb Oman for its negotiations with the Iranians to re-open the Strait of Hormuz,” he said.

“The impasse risks extending the closure of the waterway and the supply pressure it places on global energy markets, while the [hawkish](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/h/hawkish) rhetoric is forcing a greater geopolitical risk premium into prices due to a marginally higher probability of escalation in the Gulf.”

9 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 4:00 PM EDT)

## Market Close Update: Tech sags as 30Y hits 19yr high

**The U.S. markets are now closed for the day.** Here’s a look at how it all shook out across the broader universe of U.S. equities. You’ll notice there’s a lot of red out of tech and industrial land, but plenty of green in health care, staples, and energy. They dominated today’s trade, but over 59% of U.S. issues declined. The major indexes also sagged all day.

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTQ5NDc5/image.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

10 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 2:50 PM EDT)

## 30Y Treasury yield hits highest in 19 years

Earlier today, the U.S. **30Y Treasury** yield briefly eclipsed 5.337%, its highest point in nearly two decades. Here’s a look at how it has affected shares of the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF ($TLT), a common fixture of many retirement portfolios. The ETF, like other long-term bond ETFs soared to all-time highs during the zero interest rate policy of the pandemic and has subsequently sank close to its lowest point in fund history.

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTQ5MjI1/image.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

11 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 1:40 PM EDT)

## Dow Jones Today: 18 holdings advance, but index declines on $GS, $CAT weakness

The 30-strong **Dow Jones**(-0.17%) is the best-situated among major indexes today, off about a fifth of a percentage point despite 18 holdings advancing. Declines from major holdings such as $CAT are to blame.

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTQ5MTUy/image.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

13 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 12:23 PM EDT)

## Midday Movers: Winners include $AMLX, $HAE, $TRGP, $SPOT, $TEAM

At the halfway point of the day, here are the top 20 stocks in the market with at least a $2 billion market cap:

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTQ5MDY5/screenshot-2026-08-18-at-9-36-24-am.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

13 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 12:00 PM EDT)

## Midday Movers: Losers include $KLAR, $FN, $AEHR, $BIDU, $BE

Midway through the day, 55.7% of U.S. issues are declining. Here are the 20 names worst off in today’s trading with at least a market cap of $2 billion:

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTQ5MDM1/screenshot-2026-08-18-at-9-14-13-am.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

14 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 11:18 AM EDT)

## S&P 500 Today: 299 holdings advance despite tech malaise

The **S&P 500**(-0.58%) is saddling some significant declines today as tech names retreat. The rest of the index is holding up pretty firm, with 299 holdings in the green today and sectors such as health care, consumer defensive, and energy showing bright green on the index heat map:

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTQ4OTgw/image.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

By Rob Lenihan14 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 10:52 AM EDT)

## Market Movers: Ulta Beauty, Intuit, CoreWeave

Shares of energy infrastructure company Targa Resources (TRGP) climbed 6.7% following an announcement of 20-year, fee-based midstream agreements with ExxonMobil subsidiaries in the Permian Basin.

Ulta Beauty (ULTA) gained 5.1% as the largest specialized beauty retailer in the U.S. rebounded from a dip in the previous session amid positive market momentum, investor reaction to new board leadership, upcoming fall promotions and institutional buying filings.

Intuit (INTU) rose 4.4% after the tax preparation software maker expanded its Intuit Intelligence suite across its mid-market products.

On the downside, cloud computing company CoreWeave (CRWV) lost 8.3% as surging long-term Treasury yields pressured the heavily leveraged artificial intelligence infrastructure company.

Chipmaker Teradyne (TER) was down 8% as investors took profits following a 5.8% rally.

Lumentum Holdings (LITE) lost 7.7% as investors took profits amid fragile sentiment across high-multiple AI hardware and optical networking stocks.

By Rob Lenihan15 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 10:04 AM EDT)

## Disney’s (DIS) ABC Sues FCC over Alleged Retaliatory Campaign

Disney’s (DIS) ABC [filed a lawsuit alleging First Amendment violations](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/18/disney-abc-first-amendment-lawsuit-fcc.html) against the Federal Communications Commission, CNBC reported, calling the government agency’s recent investigation into the company a “retaliatory campaign” over programming that has been critical of President Donald Trump.

The network filed the lawsuit Tuesday in a district court in Washington, D.C.

The lawsuit comes months after the FCC launched an early renewal review of several ABC station licenses, citing concerns about the company’s diversity, equity and inclusion efforts.

The early review process came shortly after renewed political backlash against ABC following comments made by TV host Jimmy Kimmel on his late-night show, which airs on the network. ABC has also faced criticism from the government over its daytime talk show, “The View.”

ABC’s lawsuit calls for the FCC to halt its early broadcast license renewal proceedings.

By Rob Lenihan15 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 9:58 AM EDT)

## Mag 7 Update: Magnificent Seven ETF Falls in Early Trading

The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) fell 0.87% to $66.77 in early trading.

The ETF provides equal-weight exposure to seven major companies: Alphabet (GOOG), Amazon (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Meta Platforms (META), Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA), and Tesla (TSLA).

By Rob Lenihan16 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 9:34 AM EDT)

## Opening Bell: Stocks Fall on War Worries, Rising Oil Prices

**The U.S. stock market is now open.**

Stocks were falling in early trading as investors contended with fading hopes of resolving the U.S.-Iran conflict, surging oil prices and rising Treasury yields.

The S&P 500 was down 0.44%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged down 0.21%, and the Nasdaq lost 1.02%. The Russell 2000 gave up 0.35%.

“Markets are showing a more cautious tone today as the calm that characterized the start of the week begins to crack. U.S. equity futures are pointing lower, with the Nasdaq underperforming, as investors contend with a combination of rising long-term bond yields, renewed geopolitical uncertainty and some fresh nervousness around AI-related stocks,” said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

“The S&P 500 remains close to record highs, but the backdrop is becoming less forgiving.”

Hathorn added that the bond market is arguably the bigger story, as the U.S. 10-year yield has pushed toward 4.75%, while the 30-year has climbed above 5.3%, its highest since 2007.

“This is happening despite softer recent economic data reducing expectations for an imminent Fed hike,” she said. “Instead, the long end is responding to persistent inflation risks, heavy government borrowing and growing competition for capital—including debt issuance associated with the AI investment boom.”

“That creates an uncomfortable environment for equities because financial conditions can tighten even without the Fed raising rates,” Hathorn noted. “Geopolitics is adding to that pressure.”

By Rob Lenihan16 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 9:04 AM EDT)

## Iran War News: Iran Not Interested in Deal, Kushner Says; Tehran Threatens Offensive Posture

Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and envoy, told Fox News on Monday that Iran is “ [not showing any interest](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/us-iran-war-deal-strait-of-hormuz/)” in striking a deal that “makes sense” for the United States, CBS News reported.

Trump is focused on exerting economic pressure on Iran and ensuring it cannot build a nuclear weapon, Kushner added.

The comments came on the same day the 60-day negotiation period agreed to in the memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran expired.

Meanwhile, Iran will shift [to a “fully offensive” military posture](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-threatens-go-offensive-strait-hormuz-if-diplomacy-with-us-fails-2026-08-17/) because efforts to negotiate a permanent end to the war with the U.S. have stalled, a senior Iranian official told Reuters.

Progress toward peace talks and a resumption of oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz has ground to a halt, threatening to extend the conflict that the U.S. and Israel launched with attacks on Iran on Feb. 28.

“Iranian entities must be prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and wider region, as Iran will be ready to make decisions and take action on difficult decisions,” the official said, adding that Tehran would conduct a “timely and precise” military attack to break the U.S. naval blockade if diplomacy failed.

By Rob Lenihan16 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 8:46 AM EDT)

## Premarket Movers: DXC Technology, Bath & Body Works, Bio-Rad Laboratories

IT services and consulting company DXC Technology (DXC) shares gained 4.5% as the stock continued its technical recovery amid investor reaction to its multi-year AI turnaround strategy and new artificial intelligence partnerships.

Bath & Body Works (BBWI) climbed 3.2% after Citi analysts upgraded the retail chain to buy from neutral ahead of its second-quarter report, which is scheduled for Aug. 27.

Paylocity Holding (PCTY) rose 3.1% as investors continued to respond positively to the HR software maker’s early August fiscal fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 earnings beat.

On the downside, Bio-Rad Laboratories (BIO) tumbled 32.4% amid institutional selling, broader macroeconomic headwinds and a technical correction following a sharp short-term run-up.

Optical components maker Fabrinet (FN) sank 11.3% despite posting stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter results, as investors focused on weaker margins, negative free cash flow and a softer near-term profit outlook.

Wolfspeed (WOLF) shares sank 7.6% amid investor concerns about persistent negative margins ahead of the semiconductor company’s Aug. 19 earnings report.

By Rob Lenihan17 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 8:05 AM EDT)

## Chip Stocks Fall on Bond Yields, Mid-East Tensions

Semiconductor stocks were falling in premarket trading amid surging global bond yields, escalating Middle East tensions involving the U.S. and Iran, and profit-taking following a massive AI-driven rally.

Micron Technology (MU) was down 4%, SanDisk (SNDK) fell 4.4%, Western Digital (WDC) lost 5.4%, and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) dropped 3.3%.

“The chip strength stalled in Asian trade overnight and the losses extended through Europe,” said TheStreet Pro contributor [James “Rev Shark” DePorre](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/4-issues-are-colliding-to-test-a-vulnerable-market). “The underlying action, and particularly the bonds, indicates that the challenges are building.”

“The drivers are a combination of concern about government spending, the lack of any progress in the Middle East, and pricing pressures in AI infrastructure,” he added.

By Rob Lenihan18 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 7:35 AM EDT)

## SpaceX Shares Fall on $60 Billion Acquisition

SpaceX (SPCX) shares dropped 2.2% to $143.04 in premarket trading completing its $60 billion acquisition of Cursor, an AI-powered code editor that helps programmers write, debug and automate software development.

Elon Musk’s aerospace and AI company debuted at $135 apiece on June 12 and climbed to a record $225.64 on June 16.

Following the acquisition, Deutsche Bank analysts reiterated their Buy rating on SpaceX and $235 price target.

Among other things, the firm said the deal gives SpaceX an established presence across many blue-chip enterprises that are already using Cursor at large scale.

The agreement also gives SpaceX access to a proprietary data flywheel derived from more than 1 million real-world users generating coding interactions, which in turn represent high-quality reinforcement-learning data for models.

The deal also vertically integrates the application and harness layer, Cursor, with a frontier model, Musk’s chatbot Grok, and a large amount of computing power.

By Rob Lenihan18 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 7:08 AM EDT)

## Oil Market Update: Prices Mixed on U.S.-Iran Concerns

Oil prices were mixed in early trading as hopes faded for a settlement of the U.S.-Iran conflict.

West Texas Intermediate crude climbed 0.40% to $84.84 per barrel, while Brent crude slipped 0.18% to $90.71 per barrel.

“The lack of any kind of deal will have an impact on oil price expectations further out in 4Q and even in 2027,” said DBS Bank’s head of energy research Suvro Sarkar, [according to Reuters.](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/oil-climbs-fading-us-iran-peace-hopes-raise-supply-risks-2026-08-18/)

A projectile struck a vessel transiting out of the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday in the latest attack that has kept crossings to the single digits, despite a slight rise from the weekend, tracking data showed.

By Rob Lenihan18 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 6:55 AM EDT)

## What is the price of silver on Tuesday, August 18, 2026?

Silver futures fell 1.50% to $65.24 an ounce in early trading.

By Rob Lenihan18 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 6:53 AM EDT)

## What is the price of gold on Tuesday, August 18, 2026?

Gold futures fell 0.47% to $4,452.70 an ounce in early trading.

By Rob Lenihan18 hours ago (Aug 18, 2026 6:41 AM EDT)

## What time does the stock market open and close on Tuesday, August 18, 2026?

The U.S. stock market opens at 9:30 a.m. ET and closes at 4:00 p.m. ET.

# How major US stock indexes fared Tuesday 8/18/2026

![How major US stock indexes fared Tuesday 8/18/2026](https://media.king5.com/assets/AssociatedPress/images/d1edc151-d0a1-4cae-b103-b7a5fff03715/20260818T204005/d1edc151-d0a1-4cae-b103-b7a5fff03715_750x422.png)

How major US stock indexes fared Tuesday 8/18/2026

Wall Street pulled further from its all-time high Tuesday as AI stocks got back to sinking.

The S&P 500 fell 0.7% for a third straight modest loss since setting its all-time high on Thursday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.2%, and the Nasdaq composite sank 1.3%.

Nvidia, Micron Technology and Broadcom were some of the heaviest weights on the market amid criticism that their prices shot too high in the frenzy around AI.

Treasury yields held relatively steady in the bond market, while stock indexes were mixed in Europe and Asia.

On Tuesday:

The S&P 500 fell 53.30 points, or 0.7%, to 7,691.76.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 116.38 points, or 0.2%, to 53,343.40.

The Nasdaq composite fell 355.20 points, or 1.3%, to 26,289.71.

The Russell 2000 index of smaller companies fell 39.65 points, or 1.3%, to 3,017.89.

For the week:

The S&P 500 is down 94 points, or 1.2%.

The Dow is down 389.01 points, or 0.7%.

The Nasdaq is down 439.45 points, or 1.6%.

The Russell 2000 is down 50.53 points, or 1.6%.

For the year:

The S&P 500 is up 846.26 points, or 12.4%.

The Dow is up 5,280.11 points, or 11%.

The Nasdaq is up 3,047.72 points, or 13.1%.

The Russell 2000 is up 535.98 points, or 21.6%.
